title: Ctrl + Alt + Dungeon — I built a playable game in about a day using Google Playground's AI prompting tools (5 years of game dev experience)
author: o_perez3
selftext:
I've been working on **Ctrl + Alt + Dungeon**, a game I recently put together using Google Playground and its AI prompting tools. What really surprised me wasn't just what the AI could do, but how quickly I was able to turn an idea into something playable.

For some context, I've spent the last **5 years developing games**, mostly understanding what goes into making a game work and wearing all the different hats that come with being a solo developer. Programming, design, balancing, troubleshooting, polishing, and everything in between.

After spending some time with these AI tools, I managed to create something I'm genuinely excited about in roughly a day. Normally, getting to this point on my own would have taken considerably longer.

That said, I don't think AI is at the point where you can simply type a prompt and expect it to produce an outstanding game from start to finish.

You still have to know what you're trying to build. You have to dial in your prompts, iterate on the results, troubleshoot problems, and spend time refining the experience. Things break, features don't always work as intended, and sometimes you have to rethink your approach entirely.

In my experience, **AI doesn't eliminate the work of game development; it changes how quickly you can get through certain parts of it.** Having some development experience makes a huge difference because you need to recognize what's working, what's broken, and what needs improvement.

What used to take me considerably longer as a solo developer was possible in a fraction of the time. And that's the part I find exciting, but scary also.

I'm sharing *Ctrl + Alt + Dungeon* because I think it's a cool example of what's becoming possible with these tools, even with their current limitations. I'm also curious to see how far I can take the project.

I'm not claiming AI did everything for me, or that we're at the point where game developers are no longer needed. I'm interested in experimenting with the technology and seeing how it can help developers bring their ideas to life faster.

**I'd love to hear what other developers think:** Have you experimented with AI-assisted game development? Has it genuinely sped up your workflow, or have you found yourself spending just as much time fixing its mistakes?

And if you're interested in checking out *Ctrl + Alt + Dungeon*, I'd appreciate you taking a look!
